examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Extrema can occur at stationary points, nondifferentiable points or endpoints. Positive-to-negative derivative change indicates a local maximum; the opposite gives a minimum. A nonzero second derivative supplies a sufficient test; a zero second derivative is inconclusive. Global extrema require comparing values at all candidates, not merely solving f′=0. Check that candidate points belong to the specified domain.

**Key relationship:** At f′(a)=0: f″(a)>0 → local minimum; f″(a)<0 → local maximum

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. List stationary points, corners and endpoints.
2. Classify using derivative signs.
3. Compare values for global extrema.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Find stationary points from f′=0 and nondifferentiable interior candidates separately. Classify by a derivative sign change or, when nonzero, the second derivative. A zero second derivative is inconclusive. Global extrema on a closed interval also require endpoint values; local and global questions are not interchangeable.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
For f(x)=x³−3x, what is the difference between its local maximum value and local minimum value?

**Answer: 4.** f′=3x²−3 vanishes at ±1. f″=6x is negative at −1 and positive at 1. Values are f(−1)=2 and f(1)=−2, so the difference is 4.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A stationary point can be neither maximum nor minimum, as with x³ at zero. An unbounded open domain need not attain a global extremum.

Checking only stationary points misses endpoint extrema on a closed interval.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

For x³ at zero, the point is:

- **A.** Not stationary
- **B.** Local maximum
- **C.** Local minimum
- **D.** Stationary but not an extremum

**Answer: D.** f′(0)=0, but x³ increases through zero; no derivative sign change creates an extremum.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

For global extrema on a closed interval, consider:

- **A.** Interior stationary points
- **B.** Interior nondifferentiable points where defined
- **C.** Endpoints
- **D.** Only points with positive second derivative

**Answer: A, B, C.** Corners and endpoints can be extrema. D misses maxima and degenerate second-derivative cases.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

Maximum of x(6−x) on [0,6]?



**Answer: 9.** Complete the square: 9−(x−3)²≤9, attained at 3; endpoints give zero.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2023 CS · Q28 · MSQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/maxima-minima?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Maxima and minima. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. For f(x)=x³+15x²−33x−36, f′(x)=3(x−1)(x+11), so stationary points are −11 and 1.
2. f″(x)=6x+30. At −11 it is −36<0, giving a local maximum; at 1 it is 36>0, giving a local minimum.
3. Therefore both existence assertions **B,D** are true; A and C are false.
